# Establishment log — popol-vuh-004 (images 0019–0021)

Read 2026-11-24 from source/pages/i0019 (from line 3), i0020 and the first 13 lines of i0021, in strips at
1–1.4× with 2–2.5× crops of every doubtful word, checked word by word against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines
19275–19745). Image 0018 is blank (see popol-vuh-003's log). Start: `Cax xiban chique` (0019, line 3, right
after `xcute qui vach.`). End: `… ta xbanatahic vinac rumal Ahꜯac, Ahbit.` (0021, line 13). The next
paragraph, `Vae v xe v chacatahic v yicoxic chi puch v ꜫih Vucub Caquix cumal e caib ꜭaholab …`, begins the
story of the two boys against Vucub Caquix and belongs to popol-vuh-005.

Cut: parts.json planned 0018–0020; the part runs to 0021 line 13 so that it ends at an episode boundary
(Vucub Caquix's boast and the sentence that announces his death) rather than mid-sentence at the foot of
0020 (`mana ronohel ta | vxecah copon vi vvach`). popol-vuh-005 starts on 0021 line 13.

## Folios
The crops of 0014, 0016, 0020 and 0022 carry a number at the top left of the K'iche' column (3, 4, 5, 6);
0019 and 0021 carry none. With 0009 = fol. 1r (conventions) these are the versos?—or, if the numbers are
recto foliation, every earlier cite is one page off. Kept the count the earlier parts use (0019 = 5r,
0020 = 5v, 0021 = 6r): `fols. 5r–6r`. Logged in QUESTIONS.md.

## Letter rule used (002/003's rules, unchanged)
- q-shaped letter where Brasseur has g → ꜫ, u dropped: `hutaꜫih` ×2, `xꜫec`, `amaꜫel` ×2, `ꜫih` ×6 (incl.
  `mahabi ꜫih`, `in vꜫih`, `in ꜫih vi`, `are ta ꜫih`), `chi ꜫihil`.
- tresillo (ɛ/3-shape) → ꜫ: `ꜫaa` ×2 (the grinding stones), `pa ꜫaꜫ taꜫal` (B. gag tagal).
- g-shaped letter → ꜭ: `ꜭo pa` ×2 (B. qo), `ꜭoy` ×2 (B. qoy), `xꜭohe`, `vꜭoheic`, `quiꜭohe`, `Ꜭo nabe`,
  `zaquil ꜭahol`; gh → ꜭh: `xꜭha` ×4, `xeꜭha`, `xꜭhau`, `xꜭhauic`, `coh ꜭhauic`, `que ꜭhaquix`
  (B. chakix — the image has gh), `Ca ꜭha`, `Ꜭha ri`.
- plain c kept where Brasseur has q, k or g: `xoh coconic` (B. qokonic), `ca chucab` (B. chugab), `ca bac`,
  `chuvi cac` (B. gag), `coh icato` (B. qato), `xca nao`, `qui xcub` (B. qixcub), `vcayohic` (B. gayohic),
  `xcutuxic`, `xcohic`, `zacnatanoh`, `tocol` (B. togol), `nu calibal` ×2 (B. galibal), `ca zaquir oc`,
  `chi cutun oc`, `raxa cuval` (B. quval).
- q with u where Brasseur has q/k kept qu: `Naquipa`, `quechelah`, `riquil`, `chi iquil`, `qui quiloc`,
  `Caquix`.
- ß-ligature: ti where Brasseur has ti (`xchitih` ×2, `itiohil`, `qui tiohil`); ꜯ in tz' words (`vinac ꜯac`
  ×3, `Ahꜯac` ×2); ꜩ otherwise (`qui ꜩi`, `ri ꜩi`, `e ꜩixel`, `e ꜩalaꜩoxel`, `oh ꜩacal`, `que ꜩac`,
  `nu ꜩam`, `quiꜩih`).
- loop-t (h-like) read t, as in 003: `xoh itio`, `xquix cati chic`, `xquix catio`, `xcute`, `xcutuxic`,
  `xa ca tiltotic` (MS looks `cahiltotic`).

## Doubtful readings
- `xquix cati chic` (0019): the MS has `xquixcah` + dot + `chic`; read as loop-t + i (B. x-qu'yx qati chic).
- `cac chiquech` (0019): plain c twice; B.'s OCR is garbled (`сад`). His French reads "leurs chiens et leurs
  poules", i.e. he took the word as ac 'fowl, turkey' after qui ꜩi. Meaning uncertain; printed as written.
- `xchicaqueech` (0019): double e in the image (B. queeh).
- `coh izac pu vloc` (0019): the letter is z (ʒ), not the ligature; B. tzak. Printed z.
- `coh icato` (0019): the letter after `ca` is the ß-ligature, which elsewhere stands for ti or tz; B. qato
  ('burn'); printed t, doubtful.
- `malihab` (0019): the l and h are retraced in heavy ink; the letters can also be taken as `mahlab`. B. malihab.
- `que rah oc` (0020, line 1): the e of `que` looks like o (`quorah`); printed que as on 0019 (`querah` ×2).
- `vinac ꜯac` (0020, Vucub Caquix's speech): the final c is retraced as a heavy L-shape (a blot or correction).
- `ri xbutic` (0020): the MS has `rÿ` (r + y with diaeresis); B. riy. Printed ri, the article.
- `Ma ca quiꜩih` (0020): the image reads `maca`; B. `Ma-cu`. Printed as the image.
- `Vvcub` (0020, twice) against `Vucub` (0021, twice): printed as written; v and u are one letter in
  Ximénez's hand.
- `nimal icouen` (0021): clear in the image; B. `nimaliqouen`. Meaning uncertain.
- `ta quinel vloc` (0020): one word in the MS; B.'s OCR garbled here.

## Word division (ours)
x + absolutive kept apart from the stem as in 003 (`xoh coconic`, `xix nauic`, `xquix catio`, `xca nao`,
`coh mucunic`); future x(chi)- written as one word as in the pilot (`xchitih`, `xchicaqueech`,
`xchicahoc`, `xchicabyih`); 2nd-plural i- joined (`ivumal`, `itiohil`, `icuxih`, `icato`), as in 002/003.
Paragraphs follow Ximénez's stops and Brasseur's paragraphing; each speech is kept in one paragraph so that
the quotation marks close within it. The large capital A of `Are cut xa hubic` (0020) begins the Vucub
Caquix episode as its own paragraph. No supralinear words in this stretch.
